messages:
Stephanie Nguyen: Quick field feedback from today’s live demo (standard tenant) w/ Vectra SaaS. Overall went well, but a bunch of repeat questions came up + we were missing a couple assets in the moment. Dropping notes here so we can tighten v1.

Stephanie Nguyen: Qs they asked (in order):
1) “What happens if this model is down / capacity constrained?” (wanted something more concrete than ‘we have fallbacks’)
2) “Where do logs go? Are prompts stored?” (security person joined late)
3) “Can we keep everything in EU only?” (they have some EU users)
4) “What’s your retention by default? Can we set it to 0?”
5) “How do 429s work?” (they hit a throttle once during the demo when we re-ran the streaming scenario)
6) “Do you support SSO/SAML + RBAC? Who can view audit logs?”

Stephanie Nguyen: What we were missing:
- A single link I can paste in-chat to the security FAQ (I couldn’t find it quickly)
- A 1-slide visual for routing/fallback policy (hosted → dedicated → alt model variant) that’s easy for non-ML folks
- A canned answer on EU data residency that’s accurate for the demo tenant (what region it’s in, what we can/can’t promise)
- A ‘what to say’ on nondeterminism/output variance (they asked why the answer changed slightly on rerun)

Markus Klein: +1 on all of this. The fallback question is coming up basically every call. We should have a 60s “here’s the policy + what you’ll see in Console” talk track.

Markus Klein: On the 429: was it the tenant-wide quota or route-level? If you remember approx timestamp I can pull Console events.

Stephanie Nguyen: It was right after we toggled from Hosted route to Dedicated route for the latency comparison. Re-ran the curl script twice pretty fast. Got `429 rate_limit_exceeded` once, then it worked on retry.

Renee Sullivan: That sounds like the route-level burst limit we set low for safety. We can bump for demo tenant + keep a hard cap on tokens/day. I’ll sync w/ @Cole Summers but we should avoid seeing ANY 429s in a live demo unless we’re explicitly demoing quotas.

Soojin Lee: Re missing links: we should put “pasteables” at the top of the talk track doc (security FAQ, reset checklist, quickstart repo). Right now they’re buried.

Soojin Lee: Also: we need a cleaner phrase for “we don’t store prompts” vs “we have logs for debugging.” People hear “logs” and assume full payload retention.

Naomi Feldman: Agree. We need consistent language:
- Demo tenant: sanitized, no customer data, logging is on but we can describe what fields are captured.
- Product: configurable retention + redaction options (and Private has customer-managed logging/audit export).

Naomi Feldman: For the demo, we should NOT claim “0 retention” unless we actually have it set. Better: “configurable; in the demo tenant we retain minimal operational logs for X days; content logging is disabled / redacted.” (whatever is true)

Simran Kaur: On nondeterminism: we should just be explicit:
- “LLMs are probabilistic; we fix the seed/temperature in scripted scenarios to keep output stable”
- If we run live with temp>0, we narrate “you’ll see slightly different wording, but structure stays the same.”

Simran Kaur: We can add a ‘golden outputs’ snippet in the scenario scripts + a note: “If output diverges, pivot to expected output screenshot.”

Isabelle Laurent: For EU question: do we have a blessed one-liner for “demo tenant is in us-west; for EU-only we can do Dedicated/Private in EU regions” without overcommitting?

Lukas Meyer: (jumping in from EMEA) This comes up constantly here. We need a slide/appendix that says:
- Hosted: regions available (list)
- Dedicated/Private: region pinning + customer VPC
- Demo tenant: where it’s running + what we can show today

Lukas Meyer: Even if it’s just “ask us; we’ll confirm availability” + the supported regions list. Right now AEs improvise.

Colin O'Donnell: On the 429 + reruns: our demo curl scripts retry fast and the streaming example opens 2 connections if the terminal gets weird. We can make the scripts more “demo-safe” (sleep between runs, clearer output, detect 429 + print friendly message).

Markus Klein: Actionable asks:
1) Add a simple routing/fallback diagram + 1 slide in deck
2) Add “security FAQ” and “data residency” pasteable links at top of talk track
3) Update demo tenant quotas so we don’t accidentally hit 429 during standard scenarios
4) Add nondeterminism guidance + golden outputs fallback

Stephanie Nguyen: Yes. Also: they asked “what’s your SLA on Dedicated” and I didn’t have a safe answer beyond “contractual.” We probably need a standard range + how to position it (without putting numbers on slides).

Soojin Lee: We can add an appendix note: “SLA-backed uptime and latency targets available on Dedicated; specifics depend on commit/region.” + a “what we say vs what we show” callout.

Naomi Feldman: For the security person: they also asked “audit logs: what events?” We should have a screenshot or list (login, key changes, route changes, role changes) + who can access. If we can’t show the real audit log UI in demo tenant, at least have a static screenshot.

Renee Sullivan: I can compile the pasteables + put them in the field enablement email too. Suggest we standardize:
- Security FAQ (Confluence)
- Demo Tenant Reset Checklist (Drive)
- Sales Demo Quickstart (repo)
- “If asked: data residency” snippet

Isabelle Laurent: + for CRM workflow, we should add: when a prospect hits “EU-only / retention=0 / SOC2” you can tag “Private/Dedicated eval” and use the follow-up template with the right links. People are doing this ad hoc.

Markus Klein: I’ll open a quick ticket for quota tweak + script hardening. @Renee Sullivan can you own pasteables list?

Renee Sullivan: Yep. I’ll draft today and post here for review.

Soojin Lee: I’ll update the talk track header + add a “branch: security join late” section. That happened to me too—need a clean 2-min security recap without derailing.

Stephanie Nguyen: One more: they asked “can you show token-level cost for this single request?” We fumbled around in Console and it took too long to find the view.

Colin O'Donnell: That’s a clickpath problem. We should have a saved view called “Demo: cost breakdown (last 15m)” pinned. Also a screenshot in the deck.

Simran Kaur: Or build the scenario so after the request we immediately jump to the pre-filtered dashboard link (deep link). No hunting.

Markus Klein: Perfect. I’ll ping @Chloe Martin separately to pin the saved view and confirm the deep link is stable.

Naomi Feldman: Please make sure any deep link doesn’t expose internal-only query params that look scary to prospects (like raw IDs). If it does, screenshot instead.

Stephanie Nguyen: Cool. Thanks all. Net: demo story resonated, but we need faster “proof” assets for fallback + security + residency, and avoid 429 surprises.

Renee Sullivan: Posting draft pasteables here (WIP):
- Security FAQ: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/x/demo-tenant-security-faq
- Demo reset checklist: https://drive.google.com/redwood/demo-tenant-reset-checklist
- Standard demo deck (latest): https://drive.google.com/redwood/standard-demo-deck-working
- Talk track (speaker notes): https://drive.google.com/redwood/talk-track-standard-demo
- Quickstart template: https://github.com/redwood-quickstarts/sales-demo

Renee Sullivan: If anyone has better canonical links, reply. I’ll move these into the talk track header + enablement email.

Markus Klein: (reaction :thumbsup: x3)

Lukas Meyer: (reaction :eyes: x1) I’ll review the EU wording before it goes out. Need to keep it tight.

Soojin Lee: (reaction :white_check_mark: x1) I’ll incorporate this into the next talk track draft and flag the “what we can show live vs claim” areas.

Stephanie Nguyen: Awesome. Closing the loop: I’ll send the prospect follow-up tomorrow w/ security FAQ + quickstart once we confirm links.
